MUJAHID:v1p375#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p375#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p375#4/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses multahad as a refuge.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r1.claim: The Prophet must tell Meccan unbelievers what was revealed about the youths, without adding or subtracting.

MUQATIL:18:27-28/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:27-28/r2.claim: No one changes God's words; the Prophet must not say more about the youths than he was told, and has no refuge from God if he does.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r5.claim: No one will rule in the Hereafter contrary to God's word in this life; this is linked to God's statement that His word does not change.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses 'a refuge besides Him' as a protector or patron.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#3/r1.claim: Qatada glosses multahad as a refuge.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#4/r1.claim: Multaḥad means a place to turn aside; it derives from alḥada or laḥada, “to incline.”

TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r1.claim: The Prophet is to recite and follow the revealed Book, obeying its commands and prohibitions and practicing its lawful and forbidden rulings, or face the consequence of disobedience.

TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p234#3/r2.claim: No one can alter God’s announced words of threat against sinners who oppose the revealed Book.

TAB-FULL:v15p235/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r1.claim: ملتحدا means a place of refuge or escape; the Prophet could find nowhere to turn from God’s warning because divine power encompasses all creation.

TAB-FULL:v15p235/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses ملتحدا as a refuge.

TAB-FULL:v15p235/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses ملتحدا as a refuge or place of recourse.

TAB-FULL:v15p235/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p235/r4.claim: The word is an iftiʿāl form from laḥd, turning toward a side; laḥd names the side niche of a grave, and ilḥād in religion means turning away from it.

ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p280/r1.claim: ملتحدا means a place to turn aside to or refuge; no escape exists from God's commands and prohibitions, and no one alters His reports or commands.

THALABI:v6p165/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r10.claim: Other glosses for multahadan are a way to turn aside or a place of return.

THALABI:v6p165/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r11.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p165/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses multahadan as a place of refuge; its root relates to inclining, as with the side niche of a grave.

THALABI:v6p165/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r5.claim: The Prophet is told to recite the Qur'an and follow its contents; the author glosses the unchangeable words as God's Book.

THALABI:v6p165/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p165/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says no one can alter the Qur'an.

THALABI:v6p165/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r7.speaker: محمد بن جرير
THALABI:v6p165/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Jarir says the unchangeable words are God's threats against those who disobey Him and His Book.

THALABI:v6p165/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p165/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses multahadan as a refuge or protection.

THALABI:v6p165/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p165/r9.claim: Al-Hasan glosses multahadan as an entrance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r2.claim: A poet uses ملتحد to mean escape or a way of flight from God's decree.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r3.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r3.claim: ملتحدا may mean a deviation or alternative course.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p300/r4.claim: ملتحدا may mean a protector or ally.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r9.claim: Recitation of revelation consoles the Prophet through changing circumstances, like a beloved's letter that heals its recipient.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r1.claim: No one can alter God's words or decree; the rejected cannot be accepted, while those brought near cannot be barred from reaching Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r1.claim: “Recite what was revealed” means follow the Quran.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the words as what God has foretold, which cannot be changed; the promise, ruling, and command are included.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi takes “His words” to mean the Quran, which no one can alter.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r5.claim: Mujahid and al-Farra gloss mul tahad as refuge; al-Wahidi says refuge also derives from the notion of leaning toward something.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses “mul tahad” as a place of turning aside.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says there is no way to turn aside from God's commands and prohibitions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r8.claim: The root carries the sense of leaning: even seeking refuge means turning toward something; the same root appears in the verse about the tongue they incline to.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p597/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says no refuge or protector can be found besides God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r3.claim: The Prophet should follow the Qur'an revealed to him; no one can change God's words, and he will find no refuge apart from God.

JISHUMI:v6p4395/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r5.claim: Exception with إلا or غير affects the statement by agreement: a part may be excluded, not the whole; small or large parts are allowed, though some disallow excluding a majority, and exclusions may be nested successively.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r1.claim: Most scholars say an attached إن شاء الله removes the effect of the statement.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r2.speaker: الحسن وطاووس
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r2.claim: They allow the exception while the speaker remains in the same sitting.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r3.claim: They allow making the exception as late as a year afterward, even after the commitment has been broken; the author says this conflicts with consensus and would destabilize contracts, oaths, and divorce declarations.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r4.claim: The author rejects allowing an exception after a year or after breach, since that would keep contracts, oaths, and divorce declarations from settling.

JISHUMI:v6p4396/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4396/r6.claim: Multaḥad is a refuge or escape, derived from inclining toward a side; ilḥād is deviation from the truth.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r10.speaker: ابن جرير
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r10.claim: He says no one can alter God's promise or threat.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r11.claim: Another view includes both the wording and the meaning conveyed by God's words.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r12.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس والحسن والأصم وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r12.claim: They explain ملتحدا as refuge, shelter, fortress, an entry for escape, or a place to turn aside.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r7.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r7.claim: He takes ‘recite what was revealed’ to mean the account of the cave youths, whose truth cannot be changed.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r8.claim: He reads the command as a general, newly initiated instruction, rather than one limited to the cave story.

JISHUMI:v6p4397/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r9.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v6p4397/r9.claim: He says no one can alter the wording of the Qurʾān.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r1.claim: The Prophet is to recite and follow the Qur'an; no one can change its words, or, by another view, alter its threats to sinners.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r2.claim: He says no one can alter the Qur'an.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that no one can alter the promised threats against sinners.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r4.claim: He glosses multaḥad as a refuge or fortification.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r5.claim: He glosses it as an entrance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r6.claim: He glosses it as a refuge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r7.claim: Other glosses are a way of escape or a place of deviation; its root conveys turning aside.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r1.claim: When opponents ask for a different Qur’an or alteration, the Prophet is told to recite what was revealed and disregard their demand; no one can change God’s words, though God alone can do so.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p670/r2.claim: “You will find no refuge apart from Him” means there is nowhere to flee if one intends to comply with their demand.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r3.claim: If the previous reading is a prohibition against associating partners, 'recite' continues it; if it is an indicative statement, this verse begins a new command.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r4.claim: The command may continue the reproach over forgetting the exception: answer the questions by reciting God's revelation, follow it in practice, and recount what was revealed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r5.claim: Multahad means a refuge or side to lean toward; lahd names the slant in one side of a grave, and ilhad is deviation from truth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r6.claim: 'None can alter His words' does not deny abrogation: it either means no one but God can alter them or refers to reports and other words not subject to abrogation; the unchanging speech is God's attribute governing destiny, while Ibn Abbas says revealed books change only through interpretation.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r10.claim: No one can alter God's revealed reports or commands; on the second reading, the phrase means none can change the ruling of His words.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r11.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:18:25-27/r11.claim: Without God and obedience to the Qur'an, a person will find no refuge; other glosses render ملتحد as shelter (Ibn Abbas), recourse (Qatada), or escape and alternative (al-Zajjaj and Abu Muslim).

TABRISI:18:25-27/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r9.claim: The Prophet is told to recite what God revealed about the Cave Companions and others, or, in another gloss, to follow and act on the Qur'an.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r1.claim: One interpretation of واتل is recite: read the Quran.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r2.claim: The second interpretation is follow: adhere to the revelation and act on it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r4.claim: ملتحدا means a way to turn aside from God's command and prohibition.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r5.speaker: غيرهم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r5.claim: Others explain it as a place toward which one turns for refuge.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p132/r6.claim: For the meaning of there being no changer of God's words, he refers readers to his earlier explanation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r1.claim: The passage from this verse through the Moses-and-Khidr story forms one discourse responding to Quraysh leaders who demanded that poor believers be expelled before they would believe.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r2.claim: God rejects the leaders' demand and makes the governing instruction steadfast recitation of the revealed Book and adherence to it, disregarding objections and obstinacy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r3.claim: The command to recite includes both reading the Book and following its guidance in practice.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r4.claim: The statement that none can change God's words may support forbidding analogical qualification of an explicit text, since the command requires acting on its apparent wording.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r5.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani's position would make the verse preclude abrogation as well.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r6.claim: Abrogation is not textual alteration: a ruling remains valid until its abrogator arrives, which functions as its endpoint.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r7.claim: The commentators agree that multahad means a refuge or place of recourse.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r8.claim: Lexicographers connect multahad to lahd and ilhad, meaning to incline; mulhid is one who inclines away from religion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97#2/r9.claim: The verse means that apart from God there is no refuge in explanation and guidance.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r1.claim: One chronology places the youths in the cave before Jesus, with their awakening in the interval between Jesus and Muhammad.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r2.claim: Another says they lived before Moses, who mentioned them in the Torah, prompting the Jews’ question to the Prophet.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27#2/r3.claim: A third view places their cave entry after Jesus; the author leaves which chronology is correct to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r1.claim: The command to recite may conclude the Cave story: follow the Qur’an, for God’s words cannot be changed and His account of the youths will not fail.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r2.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r2.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the unchangeable words as God’s threats against sinners who oppose His Book.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r3.claim: If the Prophet does not follow the Qur’an and opposes it, he will find no refuge apart from God.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r4.claim: Multaḥad derives from inclination: one who seeks refuge has turned toward the place sought.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r5.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر عبد الرحيم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri identifies this verse as the end of the Cave Companions’ story.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r6.claim: When Muawiya wanted to uncover the cave, Ibn Abbas objected that God had barred someone better than him, citing the warning that an observer would flee; a wind drove out the men sent in.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r7.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:27/r7.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi also relates an elaborate report in which the Prophet sends Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali to the youths by a wind; they enter, convey his greeting, and the youths accept Islam before returning to sleep until the Mahdi and Resurrection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r1.claim: The revealed Book is the Quran; the Prophet must recite it and not heed demands for another Quran or a replacement.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:27/r2.claim: No one but God can alter His words, and there is no refuge apart from Him if one contemplates doing so.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#3/r1.claim: Recite the revealed Qur'an and ignore their requests to change it: no one can replace or alter God's words, and there is no refuge apart from Him.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r1.claim: The particle min may mark the source of revelation, with the Book as the first tablet containing all knowledge, or explain what was revealed, with the Book as discriminating intellect.

QASHANI:18:27-29/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r2.claim: God’s words that cannot be changed are the foundations of religion: divine unity, justice, and their branches; there is no refuge apart from Him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r6.claim: After revealing the cave story, God commands the Prophet to recite all revelation; no one can alter His words, either because only He can change them or because His reported truths remain fixed while some commands are abrogated.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r7.claim: The command and warning about unalterable words allude to disputants changing and distorting the cave story; ملتحد is a refuge one turns toward.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r1.claim: The Messenger is commanded to recite and convey God's Book; its words cannot be changed, distorted, or reinterpreted away.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses a refuge as a place of shelter; Qatada glosses it as a protector or master.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir explains that if Muhammad failed to recite what was revealed, he would have no refuge from God; conveying the message is reinforced by the command in 5:67 and the warning in 28:85.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r2.claim: The Prophet must persist in reciting the revealed Book to those who seek it and trust its promise, warning, affirmation, and denial.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r3.claim: God's words cannot be changed or fail; abrogation does not count as alteration in the sense intended here.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r4.claim: The Prophet has no refuge if he falls short in conveying the message entrusted to him.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.claim: Influential men asked the Prophet to exclude poor Muslims such as Salman and Abu Dharr and seat the chiefs instead; revelation of the passage threatened them with Hell.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses ملتحد as a refuge.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ملتحد as an entrance into the earth and cites a verse by Khasib al-Dimri as Arabic evidence.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r1.claim: Recite the revelation as worship and a means of nearness, act according to it, and learn its secrets; do not heed requests for another Qur'an or a change.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r2.claim: Tilāwa is Quran recitation that follows and adheres to it, as in study and regular litanies; qirāʾa more broadly means voicing letters.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r3.claim: No one can alter God's words; the general statement is qualified by the verse about replacing one revelation with another.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r4.claim: The Qur'an and its rulings never change by addition or loss and are preserved in memory; people change across ages as knowledge and practice revert to ignorance and abandonment.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r5.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r5.claim: He found a stone promising benefit if turned over; its reverse said that someone who fails to practice known knowledge cannot seek what he does not know.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r6.claim: He condemns the innovating Ilhāmiyya, who abandon learning and the Qur'an as a supposed veil and substitute poems for the Qur'an of the spiritual path.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r7.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r7.claim: His couplet contrasts a heart weary of hearing the Qur'an with falsehood weary of God's true speech.

BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r8.speaker: إبراهيم الخواص
BURSEVI:v5p183#2/r8.claim: He names five remedies for the heart: reflective Quran reading, an empty stomach, night prayer, dawn supplication, and company with the righteous; indulgence in desire leaves spiritual illness without refuge.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r1.claim: Because the cave story was unseen to the Prophet and its inclusion signals revelation and miraculousness, God commands him to keep reciting the Quran to his companions or generally and ignore demands to replace it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.claim: The verb may instead come from “following”: obey and adhere to what was revealed.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.claim: Another connection is to the earlier prohibitions on disputing deeply and consulting the People of the Book: recite what revelation says about them, be satisfied with it, and do not prolong argument; this reading means the cave-story verses.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.claim: A weaker proposal attaches the command to “Say, God knows best,” taking the revelation to mean the report of their duration; al-Ālūsī says the intended revelation is broader, including the cave account and the rest of the Book.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r1.claim: No one can alter God's words, though He can erase or confirm what He wills; the statement's broad wording covers reports and commands, understood as the rulings of His words, as al-Ṭabrisī explains.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r2.claim: The verse does not conflict with the Quran's statement that God replaces a verse: reports cannot be abrogated because that would make them false, and al-Rāzī's claim that abrogation is not really alteration is a mistaken evasion.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r3.claim: Some restrict “His words” to God's promises to monotheists, reading the verse as reassurance that God will support the Prophet and his companions against disbelievers; al-Ālūsī finds it contextually apt but unconvincing.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r4.claim: The pronoun in “His words” most likely refers to the Book, though it can refer to the Lord; the same Lord is the more apparent referent in the following pronoun.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r5.claim: “You will find no refuge besides Him” means no place to flee to in a calamity; the term derives from leaning or turning aside, and al-Rāghib allows it to be either a place noun or verbal noun.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the refuge as an underground entrance, citing a line by Khuṣayb al-Ḍamrī; al-Ālūsī says there is no need to imagine an earthen tunnel as a hiding place.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r7.claim: Since the address is to the highest of messengers, the warning is hypothetical: neither he nor his pure companions could find refuge from God; the passage ends as a prayer for divine protection.

ELMALILI:18:27-31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders God's revealed words as unchangeable and says no refuge can be found apart from Him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r1.claim: The command to recite follows the assurance that God alone has guardianship and judgment; it answers polytheists who kept asking for other signs and requested praise in the Qur’an, as at 17:73.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r2.claim: The Prophet must recite everything revealed and disregard demands to omit disliked passages or include praise; answering one question does not oblige answering every request.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r3.claim: ‘No one can change His words’ means no one is permitted to alter them by addition or omission, including suppressing passages that expose polytheism and error.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r4.claim: The wording hints that the questioners challenged details of the story, including the number of sleepers and their duration; the same denial appears at 6:34.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p302/r5.claim: The command means to continue reciting all revelation; the relative phrase is comprehensive and excludes material never revealed, such as their requested praise.

TABATABAI:18:27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r1.claim: The passage returns to the Prophet’s grief that disbelievers reject revelation; since worldly adornment is only a trial and will become barren ground, he should continue conveying the message without distress.

TABATABAI:18:27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r2.claim: In the exegetical lexicon, multahad means a refuge or place to turn aside; “the Book of your Lord” may mean the Qurʾān or Preserved Tablet, with the latter fitting “none can change His words” better.

TABATABAI:18:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r3.claim: Because the verse resumes the pre-story argument, “recite” can coordinate with the earlier statement about earthly adornment; the unchanged words and absence of refuge then explain the command.

TABATABAI:18:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r4.claim: An alternative construes the verse as an instruction to deliver an unchangeable divine message, since a messenger has no refuge from his sender except in carrying out the mission.

TABATABAI:18:27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r5.claim: The alternative is supported by 72:22–23, where the Prophet says no one can protect him from God and he will find refuge only in conveying God’s messages.

TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.speaker: سلمان
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r6.claim: Salman reports that influential converts, including ʿUyayna ibn Badr and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, asked the Prophet to remove shabby poor Muslims such as Salman and Abū Dharr; the passage then warned them of fire.

TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:29-31/r7.claim: Al-Qummī gives a similar report naming only ʿUyayna ibn al-Ḥuṣayn; its Medina setting and related reports conflict with the passage’s Meccan context.

ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n35/r1.speaker: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani
ASAD-NOTES:18:27#n35/r1.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani used this passage, among others, to reject the doctrine of abrogation, as reported by Razi.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The next section resumes the surah's opening: after the cave story showed God helping those who serve His cause, the Prophet is told to keep reciting, direct guidance to poor companions, disregard wealthy opponents, and leave them their choice and fate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet should recite the revealed Book without being troubled by opponents' demands or stubbornness; God's unchanging law guides those who prove worthy, and only God is their helper or refuge.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r1.claim: After answers about the Cave youths and Dhul-Qarnayn, polytheists asked the Prophet to alter the Quran to support their inherited customs and beliefs; the verse rejects the demand.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:27/r2.claim: The Prophet must recite and follow revelation, cannot change God’s words, and would find no refuge from punishment if he failed to obey it.

STUDYQURAN:18:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:27/r1.claim: The verse answers Makkan demands for a different or altered Quran by instructing the Prophet to recite what was revealed.

STUDYQURAN:18:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:27/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:27/r2.claim: None alters God’s words; only God can replace one revelation with another.
